rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget -- bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -n 'Pick one scoped task' plan-mode-done-right.md -> line 73 (raw) / line 85 (expanded): '**Pick one scoped task you'd send off rather than nudge bit by bit: a real slice. Bigger than a typo-fix, smaller than an epic.**' -- a whole two-sentence lead bolded, not a <=5-word handle. Harm this rule guards against: bold monoculture that dilutes emphasis so real handles stop standing out. The file's maintainer block (grep -n 'bolded task-sizing callout' -> line 93 raw) explicitly accepts the structurally identical task-sizing bold in ## Prework as check_pedagogy.md §34-mandated, but that accept-note names only '## Prework' by location -- it does not extend to this chunk's bold line, even though the shape (a task-sizing ceiling line) and the underlying §34 rationale (task selection drives the outcome, here selecting the M3 task) look identical. The harm is plausibly absent for the same reason as the Prework instance, but that is a plausible extension, not an attested one at this locus. Filing as a rule question rather than assuming the Prework note covers it, per the harm clause's instruction not to REVISE past an unresolved accept-note question without maintainer confirmation -- reported here as the todo the maintainer can close by naming this line too.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Either extend the check_pedagogy §34 maintainer accept-note to name this ## Next line too, or have the maintainer confirm it's deliberately unattested and should flatten to a handle.
